```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```


## Question 1

```{r}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("ny_noaa")

ny_noaa
```

```{r}
nrow(ny_noaa)
ncol(ny_noaa)
```

```{r}
missing_summary =
  ny_noaa |>
  summarise(
    missing_prcp = mean(is.na(prcp)) * 100,
    missing_snow = mean(is.na(snow)) * 100,
    missing_snwd = mean(is.na(snwd)) * 100,
    missing_tmax = mean(is.na(tmax)) * 100,
    missing_tmin = mean(is.na(tmin)) * 100
  )

missing_summary |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```


The `ny_noaa` dataset contains `r nrow(ny_noaa)` observations and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables, including weather station ID, date, precipitation (`prcp`), snowfall (`snow`), snow depth (`snwd`), maximum temperature (`tmax`), and minimum temperature (`tmin`).

Missing data are a substantial issue in this dataset. Precipitation has the lowest percentage of missing values (`r round(missing_summary$missing_prcp, 2)`%), followed by snowfall (`r round(missing_summary$missing_snow, 2)`%) and snow depth (`r round(missing_summary$missing_snwd, 2)`%). Maximum and minimum temperatures have the highest missing percentages, both at `r round(missing_summary$missing_tmax, 2)`%. This substantial missingness in temperature measurements may affect subsequent analyses and visualizations.
